articles.title: Ken Paxton drops lawsuit seeking to shut down immigration aid group FIEL Houston
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: The Texas attorney general also ended his effort to dissolve Annunciation House, another immigrant-serving nonprofit, as he prepares to leave office in January.

photo.caption: Mary Schultz, 80, holds a sign that reads “Stop ICE brutality! Defeat Trump Tyranny!!” during a protest held by FIEL in Houston on Jan. 9, 2026.
photo.credit: Antranik Tavitian for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Trump’s Big Bend border wall construction can resume after U.S. Supreme Court ruling
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: In an 8-1 unsigned opinion, the justices overturned an El Paso federal judge’s order to halt construction, while the Trump administration seeks further Supreme Court review.

photo.caption: Southwest Valley employees excavate and bulldoze an area starting from the Santa Elena Canyon trailhead parking lot next to Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive in Big Bend National Park on Aug. 13, 2026.
photo.credit: Kaylee Greenlee for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Houston mayor limits police cooperation with ICE after Democratic wins
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: Houston police will stop contacting ICE during traffic stops when drivers aren’t arrested, even if they have immigration warrants. The change follows pressure from Gov. Greg Abbott to maintain cooperation.

photo.caption: People march through downtown to protest the killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo on Saturday, July 11, 2026, in Houston. Salgado Araujo was fatally shot by an immigration officer early in the morning of July 7.
photo.credit: Jon Shapley for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Texas spent billions on border security. What happens to Greg Abbott’s mission when Dems take over?
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: After Abbott’s defeat, Texas’ new governor faces questions about Operation Lone Star, border security and the future of immigration enforcement.

articles.title: After supporting Trump in 2024, Texas border counties fueled Democrats’ big night
articles.author: Colleen DeGuzman, Berenice Garcia and Alejandro Serrano, and graphics byApurva MahajanAlex Ford , Berenice Garcia, Apurva Mahajan, Alejandro Serrano, Alex Ford
articles.excerpt: Counties along the U.S.-Mexico border saw the largest surge in voter turnout compared to any other region in the state.

photo.caption: Voter turnout along the U.S.-Mexico border surged in 2026, helping Democrats like Bobby Pulido win a seat in Congress.
photo.credit: Brenda Bazán for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Texas ICE agent indicted for striking fleeing Houston pedestrian with vehicle
articles.author: Uriel J. García, Stephen Simpson
articles.excerpt: A Harris County grand jury indicted a federal immigration agent caught on video striking a pedestrian during a vehicle pursuit.

photo.caption: Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare and officials watch body camera footage during a press conference announcing a grand jury indictment of ICE agent Mario Alberto Morales on a charge of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, in Houston. The indictment alleges Morales drove his vehicle into Miguel Parra-Hernandez.
photo.credit: Antranik Tavitian for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Dolores Huerta, trailblazing advocate for migrant farmworkers, dies at 96
articles.author: Colleen DeGuzman , Jess Huff
articles.excerpt: Huerta co-founded several organizations to support Texas farmworkers. She was also an ardent advocate for women and immigrant's rights.

photo.caption: Dolores Huerta, civil rights leader and co-founder of United Farm Workers, speaks at the Texas Democratic Convention in Corpus Christi June 26, 2026.
photo.credit: Eddie Gaspar/The Texas Tribune

articles.title: U.S. Supreme Court leaves in place limits on when deportation cases can be paused
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: The court declined to block a settlement between Texas and the Justice Department that effectively restricts when judges can use their discretion in how quickly immigration cases are resolved.

articles.title: Austin man shot by ICE officer pleads not guilty to federal assault charge
articles.author: Uriel J. García, Alex Nguyen
articles.excerpt: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez entered the plea a week after a grand jury indicted him on one count of assaulting, resisting, impeding and obstructing a federal officer.

photo.caption: Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, an immigration attorney representing Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, who was shot by federal immigration agents on Sept. 20, holds a news conference following his federal bail hearing at the federal courthouse in Austin on Sept. 30, 2026.
photo.credit: Eli Hartman for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Feds may build border wall through South Texas refuge as original plan stalls in court
articles.author: Berenice Garcia
articles.excerpt: The original plan, which has been stalled since July, called for construction of a wall along the Santa Ana wildlife refuge.

photo.caption: Survey stakes mark the proposed location of the border wall at the Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge near Alamo on July 8, 2026.
photo.credit: Gabriel V. Cárdenas for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Trump administration can hold immigrants in ICE custody without bond, court rules
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled detained immigrants don’t have a constitutional right to a bond hearing after they enter the country illegally.

photo.caption: The entrance to the Bluebonnet Detention Center in Anson on Aug. 22, 2026. The privately run immigration detention center is operated by Management & Training Corporation, under contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
photo.credit: Ronald W. Erdrich for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Guatemalan man gets 30 years for role in San Antonio smuggling deaths of 53 migrants
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: Rigoberto Ramon Miranda-Orozco received a 30-year prison sentence in a San Antonio migrant smuggling case that left 53 people dead.

photo.caption: 53 migrants died in an abandoned tractor-trailer found near Lackland Air Force Base in San Antonio on June 27, 2022.
photo.credit: Nick Wagner for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Dallas man who died in Laredo ICE facility was lawful permanent resident
articles.author: Colleen DeGuzman, Alex Nguyen, Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: ICE said Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias obtained his legal status fraudulently because he failed to disclose a 2004 arrest for theft. His daughter disputes that.

photo.caption: A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent’s badge is seen in front of the J.J. Pickle Federal Building in Austin on April 1, 2025.
photo.credit: Eddie Gaspar/The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Migrant found dead at Laredo ICE facility
articles.author: Colleen DeGuzman, Alex Nguyen
articles.excerpt: The death was confirmed by U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar, who said the 56-year-old Mexican national was found unresponsive in his cell. He’s the seventh person in Texas to die while detained by ICE this year.

articles.title: Harris County prosecutor to investigate ICE striking Houston man with vehicle
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: District Attorney Sean Teare said his office is investigating whether an ICE agent in an SUV intentionally struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez as he fled.

photo.caption: Harris Co. District Attorney Sean Teare speaks during an oversight hearing about the July 7 fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, in Houston on July 24, 2026.
photo.credit: Jon Shapley for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: San Antonio sues to block plans to convert warehouse into an ICE detention center
articles.author: Alex Nguyen
articles.excerpt: The city argued that federal officials failed to review the environmental impact of a proposed facility that could hold 1,500 people a day.

photo.caption: A sign reading “ICE Out of SATX” is seen at a field hearing with elected officials hearing testimony about a proposed ICE facility and immigration enforcement efforts by the federal government, in San Antonio on Oct. 2, 2026.
photo.credit: Christopher Lee for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Judge halts border barrier construction in Big Bend
articles.author: Sam Karas, Big Bend Sentinel
articles.excerpt: U.S. District Judge Kathleen Cardone’s ruling means federal contractors can’t continue construction in the national park or surrounding areas until a lawsuit opposing the work is resolved.

photo.caption: Southwest Valley employees survey an area in the parking lot of a river access area off of Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive in Big Bend National Park on Aug. 13, 2026.
photo.credit: Kaylee Greenlee for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Austin man has surgery 11 days after being shot by ICE agent
articles.author: Zach Leggio
articles.excerpt: The surgery on the Venezuelan national, who has been in custody since his Sept. 20 run-in with an immigration officer, removed the bullet lodged in his back.

photo.caption: A video of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez after he was shot by an ICE officer is shown during a news conference conducted by Austin Mayor Kirk Watson and Austin PD Chief Lisa Davis on Sept. 22, 2026, regarding the Sept. 20 shooting.
photo.credit: Jacob Lujan/The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Texas schools reported losing 14,200 immigrant kids last year. The true number is likely higher.
articles.author: Megan Menchaca
articles.excerpt: The actual enrollment loss amid increased deportation efforts is much higher as the federal definition that identifies immigrant students is limited, experts said.

photo.caption: Nimitz Middle School students take part in a class activity on Sept. 13, 2023 in Odessa.
photo.credit: Eli Hartman/The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Austin man shot by ICE agent charged with assault, resisting arrest
articles.author: Zach Leggio
articles.excerpt: In a federal criminal complaint, DHS says Wilber Rafael Garces Perez knew he was fleeing federal agents and his car’s sideview mirror struck an officer. A judge ordered him to remain in detention.

photo.caption: Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents at the scene where Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a Venezuelan man, was shot and injured in Austin on Sept. 20, 2026.
photo.credit: Jacob Lujan/The Texas Tribune

articles.title: ICE agent who shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston identified
articles.author: Lomi Kriel, Eddie Gaspar
articles.excerpt: The federal government has withheld his identification, even as major state and local law enforcement agencies across the country typically identify officers involved in shootings on the job soon after the incident.

articles.title: Cuellar and progressives form tenuous alliance amid Trump’s immigration crackdown
articles.author: Berenice Garcia
articles.excerpt: U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar is known as one of the most conservative Democrats in Congress who often diverges from the party on issues like immigration, abortion and gun rights.

photo.caption: U.S. Rep. Henry Cuéllar, D-Laredo, second from left, takes a photo with people during the LUPE Votes five year anniversary celebration at the Pharr Development and Research Center in Pharr on Aug. 29, 2026.
photo.credit: Gabriel V. Cárdenas for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Watch: Joaquin Castro, Sigrid Gonzalez and Rochelle Garza discuss Texas’ ICE detention centers
articles.author: Texas Tribune Events Staff
articles.excerpt: People who have been inside Texas’ ICE detention centers describe what’s happening, who's being held and what it means for communities, families and the rule of law at 2:15 p.m. Saturday.

articles.title: Catholic Charities leader says feds have lifted a ban on funding for the nonprofit
articles.author: Uriel J. García
articles.excerpt: Sister Norma Pimentel told a Texas Tribune Festival audience that the Rio Grande nonprofit met with government officials to clear up accusations of “major grant violations.”

photo.caption: Sister Norma Pimentel, executive director of Catholic Charities of the Rio Grande Valley, speaks during a one-on-one conversation with Niala Boodhoo, journalist and podcast host of “Oh God Now What,” at The Texas Tribune Festival on Sept. 25, 2026.
photo.credit: Eli Hartman for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: ICE shootings prompt different reactions from longtime Democrats leading Austin, Houston
articles.author: Colleen DeGuzman
articles.excerpt: Mayor Kirk Watson ordered Austin police to investigate, saying he didn’t trust the feds. Mayor John Whitmire initially said Houston lacked jurisdiction.

photo.caption: From left: Austin Mayor Kirk Watson and Houston Mayor John Whitmire.
photo.credit: Joel Angel Juarez and Jon Shapley for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Venezuelan man shot by ICE officer needs surgery to remove the bullet, U.S. Rep. Greg Casar says
articles.author: Zach Leggio, Alex Nguyen
articles.excerpt: The man was shot by a recent ICE recruit who was not wearing a body camera, according to news reports.

photo.caption: Law enforcement agents at the scene of a shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in North Austin on Sunday.
photo.credit: Jacob Lujan/The Texas Tribune

articles.title: After ICE shooting, Venezuelan man’s quick release from Austin hospital raises questions
articles.author: Uriel J. García, Zach Leggio, Alex Nguyen
articles.excerpt: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez was discharged after four hours into ICE custody and taken 135 miles to an immigration detention center.

photo.caption: A video of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez after he was shot by an ICE officer is shown during a news conference conducted by Austin Mayor Kirk Watson and Austin PD Chief Lisa Davis on Sept. 22, 2026, regarding the Sept. 20 shooting.
photo.credit: Jacob Lujan/The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Migrants who planted roots in Texas are being swept up in the immigration crackdown. Here are five of their stories.
articles.author: Uriel J. García, Alejandra Martinez, Alejandro Santos Cid and Alex Nguyen | Illustrations by Lauren Crow | Data analysis by Alex Ford , Alejandra Martinez, Alejandro Santos Cid, Alex Nguyen, Alex Ford
articles.excerpt: Some detained Texans were pursuing pathways to stay here legally. None had criminal convictions.

photo.caption: From left: Malena Chacón Santos, Yeferson Francisco Sequera Ruiz, Dixuan Li, Octavio Daniel Cabrera Valdez, Shahrokh Rahimi.
photo.credit: Lauren Crow for The Texas Tribune

articles.title: A surge of ICE arrests and the shooting of a Venezuelan man strike fear into Austin neighborhoods
articles.author: Alejandro Serrano, graphics by Alex Ford , Alex Ford
articles.excerpt: People who work near the site where ICE shot Wilber Rafael Garces Perez say the agency’s presence in the area has been constant amid President Trump’s mass deportation push.

photo.caption: Protestors fill the intersection of West Anderson Lane and Research Boulevard in north Austin after an immigration enforcement agent shot and injured Wilber Rafael Garces Perez on Sept. 20, 2026.
photo.credit: Jacob Lujan/The Texas Tribune

articles.title: Venezuelan man shot by ICE in Austin said he tried to pull over before officers fired at him
articles.author: Uriel J. García, Alex Nguyen and Zach Leggio, Alex Nguyen, Zach Leggio, Laura Duclos
articles.excerpt: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez legally entered the country in 2024 via the CBP One app and applied for asylum, his attorneys said. But he missed a court hearing after the notice went to the wrong address.

photo.caption: Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, an immigration attorney representing Wilber Rafael Garces Pérez, who was shot by an immigration officer in Austin on Sunday, listens as Garces Pérez speaks on the phone from detention at a press conference on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026.
photo.credit: Leila Saidane for The Texas Tribune
